Message End Event

General Concept: A Message End Event in BPMN is used to signal the end of a process or subprocess by sending a message to an external participant or system. It is typically used for outbound notifications or integration with other processes.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Message End Event sends a message when the process instance reaches its end. You can define output mappings using FEEL expressions to prepare the message payload. The engine supports error handling and ensures that only mapped variables are sent. Message End Events can interact with messaging systems, APIs, or custom adapters for outbound communication.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Message End Event in TaktX allows you to:

  • Define output mappings using FEEL expressions to prepare the message payload.
  • Configure error handling and delivery options for reliable notification.
  • Limit variable scope to only mapped variables for security and clarity.
  • Integrate with messaging systems, APIs, or custom adapters for outbound communication.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Attach boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling if needed.

 

Example: Support Ticket Process with Message End Event

 

This example shows a process where a support ticket is handled, and upon resolution, a Message End Event notifies the customer. The Message End Event demonstrates outbound notification at process completion.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions to format and validate message payloads.
  • Configure error handling for reliable delivery.
  • Document message formats and endpoints.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmapped variables will not be included in the message.
  • Handle delivery errors to avoid missing notifications.
  • Ensure message endpoints are reachable and properly secured.
